penetration_assumption: TWO NUMBERS, DIFFERENT CONFIDENCE. (1) ASSORTMENT ADDS = Rs 1.07 L/yr, the only genuinely-absent lines worth stocking. WHO-ORS sachets: 6% of 4,700 residents buy 2 sachets/yr at Rs 22 = 564 sachets = Rs 12,400 (suppressed because Akal Charitable Hospital hands ORS out free; stock it for service, not revenue). Bulk water 2 L/5 L PET from the Jivo plant: 5% of ~350 staff households take 1x5 L/week at Rs 60 = Rs 54,600, plus guest-house/institutional Rs 40,000 = Rs 95,000 — ESTIMATED, low confidence, because current packaged-water consumption is only 3.0 L per resident per YEAR (13.9 kL / 4,700), which says nobody here has a bought-water habit. (2) AVAILABILITY RECOVERY on the range ARY already lists = Rs 5.3 L/yr, the real prize. Method: 85 cold-drink SKUs that sold on >=20 days in Mar-Aug 2026 AND averaged >=3 units per selling day (so a zero-sale day is evidence of absence, not of low demand) earned Rs 17.73 L; at each SKU's own observed daily rate for 165 of 183 days they would have earned Rs 34.92 L — a raw gap of Rs 17.19 L. Substitution haircut, stated plainly: on a closed campus with no second shop, a resident who finds Fanta 400 ml missing mostly buys the Fanta 250 ml or the Coke that IS on the shelf, so only ~25% of a missing SKU's shortfall is genuinely lost to ARY. Evidence for high substitution: monthly category sales Mar-Aug tracked weather and the school calendar (Rs 2.23 L -> 4.30 L -> 3.36 L), not the SKU count present (89 -> 105 -> 110). 25% x Rs 17.19 L = Rs 4.30 L for the season; off-season (32% of category sales, lower demand) adds ~Rs 1.0 L. Band Rs 4.3-6.4 L at a 20-30% incremental factor. THE VERDICT IS HIGH CONFIDENCE (VERIFIED counts); THE RUPEE FIGURE IS MEDIUM — the substitution factor is the one input I could not measure directly, and it moves the answer +/-40%.
probe_evidence: Every "absent" claim below was probe-tested; the coverage diff itself reported ZERO "missing" lines out of 48, and my probes found only 5 genuinely-empty lines, 3 of which should be killed. NOTE: `ary assort probe` under zsh does NOT word-split an unquoted variable — my first probe batch returned 0 for everything including `lassi`, which I know returns 104 SKUs. Pass each term as its own argument. PROBES RUN (12-month window): `probe tonic schweppes "ginger ale"` -> 2 SKUs, both "Jivo Wheatgrass Juice 200 Ml Ginger Ale" (a wheatgrass juice, not a mixer) = NO tonic water exists. `probe "ice cube" icecube "ice pack"` -> 0 SKUs. `probe kombucha seltzer` -> 5 SKUs, all "Amul Tru Seltzer", all Rs 0 lifetime = no kombucha, seltzer listed-and-dead. `probe electral orsl enerzal prolyte walyte` -> 0 SKUs across every group = WHO-ORS sachets genuinely absent (5 Cipla/generic ORS 200 ml RTD SKUs do exist, Rs 8,161/yr). `probe gatorade sting powerade` -> 14 matched, 5 sold, Rs 7,448 — but the sales are `Cielo Basting Spoon` and `Sofy Body Fit` catching the substring; real Gatorade (5 SKUs) and Sting (4 SKUs) = Rs 0. `probe lahori banta rimzim limonata shikanji` -> 5 SKUs, 1 sold Rs 10,840 = "Jivo Wheatgrass Pet 160Ml Punjabi Shikanji"; Lahori Zeera 160/300 ml = Rs 0. `probe bisleri kinley aquafina bailley "mineral water" "drinking water" vedica himalayan` -> 21 SKUs, 8 sold Rs 3.04 L, of which Rs 2.81 L is JIVO's OWN house-brand water; Bisleri/Aquafina/Equal/Springwell/Ula all Rs 0. A full `%water%` scan of the catalogue confirms NO 2 L / 5 L / 10 L / 20 L pack exists in any group. `probe roohafza "rooh afza" sharbat thandai` -> 10 SKUs, 2 sold Rs 15,645. `probe pressery "real activ" "no added sugar"` -> 2 SKUs, 0 sold. CAUTION ON THE COVERAGE DIFF: its "covered" verdicts are as unreliable as its "missing" ones. It scored Cola at 6 SKUs / Rs 25,845 by matching the literal string "coca-cola" — ARY's SKU is "Coca Cola 250 Ml" with no hyphen and does Rs 1.05 L alone. It marked Lassi covered at Rs 18.36 L on the word "amul" (that is Amul butter/cheese/ice-cream; real lassi+chaas is Rs 55,200). It marked Kombucha covered on "neer", Ice cubes on "rock" (rock salt), Sports drinks and Glucose on "orange", Iced tea on "mango", Tonic on "ginger", Jeera soda on "masala" (spice mixes), ORS on "care" (personal care). Roughly 40% of its 48 lines are false-covered.
top_skus: DO NOT ADD SKUs — FIX THE ORDER BOOK. 471 of 670 active cold-drink SKUs sold nothing in 12 months and NOT ONE of them holds a single unit of stock; 263 have never rung a sale in the system's life.

Availability action 1 — raise the delivery cadence. The main soft-drink distributor Gian Chand Faquir Chand billed only 22 times in 12 months (Rs 12.55 L of Rs 19.0 L total category purchases) — one delivery every ~17 days into a category that sells every day. Weekly in Mar-Aug is the single highest-value change in this category.

Availability action 2 — 101 of the 199 SKUs that sold in the last 12 months have ZERO or negative stock right now. Reorder these eight first, all proven sellers now at zero: Coca Cola 740 Ml (Rs 37,735/yr), Fanta 400 Ml (Rs 35,120), Sprite 740 Ml (Rs 21,035), Coke Can 200 Ml (Rs 20,130), Frooti Mango 330 Ml (Rs 17,880), Limca 740 Ml (Rs 16,730), Parle Agro Appy Fizz 250 Ml (Rs 15,000), Pepsi Nimbooz 345 Ml (Rs 14,980).

Availability action 3 — CHAAS / LASSI is the biggest single miss and it is a buying failure, not a range failure. 17 lassi/chaas/buttermilk SKUs are listed; 6 sold anything (Rs 55,200 / 2,767 units = 0.59 units per resident per YEAR); 5 of those 6 are at zero stock today. Amul Buttermilk 200 ml Spiced last sold 2025-09-04. Verka — the culturally native Punjab Milkfed brand — has 3 SKUs, 1 selling Rs 2,700, all at zero stock. Getting chaas+lassi to 3 units/resident/yr (still far under a Punjabi household's rate) is +Rs 1.57 L/yr on SKUs ARY already lists.

GENUINELY ABSENT, WORTH ADDING (2 lines only): (a) WHO-ORS sachets — Electral 21.8 g, Prolyte, plus a 10-sachet box. Zero SKUs exist anywhere in the catalogue. Rs 12,400/yr, but it is the one non-negotiable safety line for a 4,700-person closed township 30-50 km from a real pharmacy. Stock only true WHO-formula ORS — FSSAI has pulled sugary drinks branded 'ORS' off shelves. (b) Bulk water 2 L / 5 L PET from the Jivo plant — Rs 95,000/yr, 33.5% house-brand margin.

GENUINELY ABSENT, KILL — the demand research itself says so: Tonic water / botanical mixers ('almost entirely inappropriate' — a Kalgidhar Trust township where alcohol is prohibited); Ice cubes ('do not buy packaged ice', make it on site); Kombucha ('probably skip' — Rs 100+ price point, near-zero awareness); 20 L returnable jar (needs a BIS/ISI-14543 filler within 50 km and a jar-deposit register FusionERP8 is not running).

POLICY CALL, NOT A BUYING CALL — Sting 250 ml at Rs 20 (4 SKUs listed, Rs 0) would sell, but FSSAI's 2026 order caps caffeine and strips the 'energy drink' descriptor, and ARY's largest cohort is 5-18. Red Bull already does Rs 62,375/yr at the university-side counter. Net of cannibalisation Sting is worth Rs 15-25 k/yr — do not touch it without the trust's written sign-off.
blockers: MARGIN, NOT SHELF, IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT — and the demand research's assumed margin band is wrong by 2-3x. Derived live from PurchaseDetail vs SaleDetail (185 of 199 selling SKUs costed, covering Rs 28.38 L of Rs 29.76 L): carbonates earn 10.6% of MRP, juice/dairy/other packaged 16.9%, JIVO house brand 33.5%. Blended ex-house-brand = 12.9%. Worked example, VERIFIED across 17 purchase lines: Coca-Cola 250 ml lands at Rs 12.50 ex-tax + 40% GST/cess = Rs 17.50, sells at Rs 20 MRP, nets Rs 14.29 after output tax — Rs 1.79 gross profit, 8.9% of MRP. The research assumed 20-35%. At these margins Rs 5.3 L of recovered sales is only ~Rs 69,000 of gross profit, so the case for the fix is footfall and service, not category profit.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH — 17 suppliers touched the category in 12 months but one (Gian Chand Faquir Chand) carries 66% of it on 22 bills. PepsiCo's whole portfolio behaves like a distributor problem, not a demand problem: Pepsi 400 ml (Rs 12,020 in 25 days), Tropicana Slice 250 (Rs 11,400 in 26 days), Mirinda Orange 400 and Pepsi Nimbooz all sold well and then simply stopped mid-season with zero stock, while Coca-Cola's identical packs ran continuously. Fixing that is a second-source conversation, not a shelf decision.

CAPITAL AND SHELF ARE NOT BLOCKERS, AND NEITHER IS COLD CHAIN. ARY runs Rs 5.6 L of Frozen and Rs 4.3 L of chilled Dairy in the same window, so freezers and chillers exist. The category is already listed at 2.13x the external benchmark range (`ary assort benchmark`: Beverages 438 benchmark lines vs 935 active SKUs, 271 selling = 61.9%, verdict 'adequate' — the only non-gap verdict besides snacks). Adding SKUs makes the 70% dormant tail worse.

THE RUPEE FIGURE'S WEAK LINK: the 25% substitution factor. I could not measure it directly — FusionERP8 records no stock-on-hand history, so I inferred absence from zero-sale days on high-velocity SKUs and inferred substitution from category totals holding steady while individual SKUs vanished. A 20-30% band gives Rs 4.3-6.4 L. The verdict itself does not depend on that number.

FRESHNESS AND SCOPE, stated for the record: the stock audit that froze the feed at 2026-08-21 is over — sales, purchases and accounting all run to 2026-08-30 (`ary doctor`). All figures use a live 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31 window and supersede the corpus's 2026-08-21 cut. Category defined as product groups 120 Drinks + 145 Soft Drinks + 174 Shakes + 198 Milk Shake (Rs 29.76 L) plus 16 hand-verified cold-beverage SKUs the category tree filed elsewhere (Rs 3.25 L): Cold Coffee Gc under Hot Drinks (Rs 2.19 L), lassi/chaas under Dairy Products, Rooh Afza and Amul tender-coconut cups under Confectionery, Tang under General Items, Glucose-D under Medicare. Total Rs 33.0 L = 4.3% of ARY's Rs 7.67 Cr 12-month gross, Rs 702 per resident per year.
kill_reason: The assortment gap this category was supposed to contain is largely not there, and the coverage diff's own output already said so: it returned ZERO "missing" lines out of 48 and an empty mustHaveMissing array. Testing it against the live catalogue confirms that and inverts the question. VERIFIED: 714 SKUs sit in the four cold-drink groups, 670 active, and only 199 sold a single rupee in the 12 months to 2026-08-31. 471 active SKUs sold nothing — 263 of them have never recorded a sale in the system's entire history — and NOT ONE of those 471 holds any stock (`SELECT COUNT(*) ... dormant_with_stock` = 0). That is the definition of listed-but-never-bought-in. Availability, measured directly: across the 183 days of peak season (2026-03-01 to 2026-08-31) only SIX SKUs were on shelf 150+ days; 59 sold on fewer than 20 days; and 101 of the 199 12-month sellers carry zero or negative stock today. Meanwhile `ary assort benchmark` scores Beverages at 2.13x the benchmark range with 61.9% of it selling and calls the verdict "adequate" — the only category besides snacks not flagged as a range gap. Of the five lines that ARE genuinely empty, three should be killed on the research's own advice (tonic water is inappropriate on a dry Kalgidhar Trust campus; packaged ice needs a dedicated freezer for an 8-10 week hill season; kombucha is a Rs 100+ metro product with no awareness base) and a fourth (the 20 L returnable jar) is blocked on a BIS-licensed local filler and a jar-deposit register that does not exist. What is left worth adding is two lines and Rs 1.07 L. A recommendation to ADD cold-beverage SKUs here would put more stock-less listings on top of 471 that already exist. The money is in buying the range ARY already lists, more often.
